program_analysis.summary: The program implements a semi-supervised learning approach using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone for image classification. It utilizes labeled and unlabeled data to refine class prototypes through feature extraction and consistency objectives. Data augmentation techniques are applied to enhance the labeled dataset, and the model is trained using cross-entropy loss. The program is designed to predict categories for new images based on the learned prototypes.

This program implements a classification agent using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone with a focus on semi-supervised learning. It employs a two-view labeled dataset for training, utilizing data augmentation techniques and a combination of supervised contrastive loss and cross-entropy loss for optimization. The model is trained using a parameter-efficient finetuning method, allowing for effective learning with limited labeled data.

This program implements a semi-supervised learning framework for image classification using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone with DINOv2 features. It extracts features from labeled and unlabeled images, applies label propagation to generate pseudo-labels, and trains a linear head on both labeled and pseudo-labeled data. The program includes data augmentation techniques to enhance the training process and utilizes a KNN graph for effective label propagation.

This program implements a semi-supervised learning framework for image classification using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone with DINOv2 features. It combines labeled and unlabeled data through multi-view augmentations and builds a memory bank for unlabeled samples. A linear classification head is trained on the extracted features, and predictions are made by fusing global and local probabilities. The program emphasizes data-efficient training strategies and robust feature extraction.

This program implements a semi-supervised learning framework using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone for image classification. It employs a teacher-student model approach, where a teacher model provides pseudo-labels for unlabeled data. The training process includes data augmentation techniques, weighted sampling for class balance, and consistency loss to improve model robustness. The program also normalizes features to enhance performance during training and evaluation.
